account:
The town has seemed mostly routine today, but there are a few unexplained matters. At afternoon tea my neighbour repeated rumours of lights at the bakery and a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' The neighbour named Townsfolk 02 as the source outside the bakery this morning, but had seen no change personally. I have not verified any riverfront project and do not know what those words mean.

There is a definite lighting inspection tomorrow at 18:00 in the great hall. The secretary recorded it, and the innkeeper says eight lanterns have been installed to check lighting around the tables. That sounds like ordinary town business; I have no evidence linking it to the bakery rumours.

The town accounts are missing or their storage is unknown to us. I found 128 emeralds in the treasury, but no account papers. The secretary searched the four great hall table chests: three were empty and one held bread. Now the secretary has come to my home late at night to report that the builder, baker and innkeeper do not have the ledger or know where it is kept. The builder and baker have no town invoices with them. The innkeeper says a bread order is private, not a town expense. That private order may explain some bread-related activity, but I do not know its purpose or participants beyond this report. There is not enough evidence to conclude that anything improper is happening. The late visit and repeated failure to locate accounts are unusual; tomorrow I should clarify the private order if relevant and establish who actually maintains town records, while keeping my scheduled appointments.
